model: REIT Core AFFO capitalisation at cost of equity (engine route)

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Judgment: 10-year Core AFFO/share CAGR of the base path (FY2026E $7.52 -> FY2035E $10.03). Sits between the 3-year (-0.3%) and 5-year (+5.8%) Core AFFO CAGRs: the 5-year figure is inflated by the 2021-2022 Sunbelt rent surge (+21% in FY2022 alone) and the 3-year figure captures the 2023-2026 supply-wave give-back, neither of which is a run-rate. Equity CAGR is not usable for a REIT (book equity shrinks mechanically with depreciation and a >100% payout of GAAP earnings).
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (-0.9% 5yr) diverges from revenue (+5.7%) and EPS (+11.5%) by far more than 30%. Expected for a REIT: GAAP book value is depreciated historical cost and the dividend exceeds GAAP net income, so shareholders' equity declines even as the asset base and AFFO grow. Growth was therefore selected from the Core AFFO/share series, not book equity.
historical_growth.notes: Core AFFO/share has fallen three years running (FY2023 $8.24 -> FY2026E $7.50, -9%) while revenue grew ~3%/yr: the Sunbelt supply wave (2023-2025 deliveries) flattened same-store NOI (FY2026 guide -0.9%) and interest expense rose with development completions and refinancing (Q2-26 $53.1M vs $45.1M). The dividend ($6.12) is 82% of FY26E Core AFFO, up from 70% in FY2021 - coverage is intact but thinner.

scenario_narratives.base: A transitional 2026 (Core AFFO $7.50) followed by a measured Sunbelt recovery: deliveries fall below long-run averages for 2027-2029, same-store NOI returns to +3-4%, the lease-up pipeline adds ~$0.11/share, and refinancing at ~5% absorbs roughly half of that operating upside. Core AFFO/share compounds ~3.2%/yr over ten years and the dividend stays covered at ~75-80% of AFFO.
scenario_narratives.bull: The supply cliff and continued Sunbelt in-migration produce three years of mid-single-digit same-store NOI growth, development yields hold a 100bp+ spread to cap rates, and operating leverage takes the Core AFFO margin to 43%. Core AFFO/share reaches ~$9.55 by FY2030 and the market re-rates toward 18x.
scenario_narratives.bear: Rates stay above 5% on the 10-year, debt rolls at 150-200bp above the in-place coupon, construction starts recover before the supply overhang clears, and new-lease pricing stays negative through 2027. Core AFFO/share troughs ~$7.05 and the stock is valued as a 2% grower at a 15x cap; the balance sheet (4.5x net debt/EBITDAre, 87% fixed, 6-year maturities) keeps this an earnings problem, not a solvency one.

valuation_philosophy.summary: MAA is valued on the cash it can actually distribute - Core AFFO (Core FFO less recurring capex), after interest and preferred dividends - capitalised at a 9.0% USD cost of equity built off a 5.2% 10-year Treasury, with net debt NOT deducted a second time. Three explicit ten-year AFFO paths bracket the Sunbelt supply recovery and the refinancing headwind; the market price is read against where it sits between them. GAAP net income, EPS, P/E, EV/EBITDA and book equity are not used: depreciation of $620M+/yr and >100% payout of GAAP earnings make them structurally uninformative for an apartment REIT.
key_risks_to_valuation: Cost of equity: every 50bp on the 9.0% discount rate moves base value roughly 8-9%; the 5.24% 10-year Treasury reading used is high by post-2009 standards and the valuation is cheaper if rates mean-revert (and dearer if they do not)
Refinancing: $5.7B of debt at a 3.9% average coupon with 6.0 years average maturity re-prices toward 5-6% over the horizon; each 100bp on the full stack is ~$57M (~6%) of Core AFFO
Sunbelt supply timing: management has trimmed same-store revenue guidance twice in 2026; a slower-than-expected clearing of the 2023-2025 delivery overhang pushes the base path toward the bear path
Development execution: the $800M-$1B pipeline and $624M lease-up book carry lease-up, concession and cost risk; the model assumes stated yields are achieved
Share count: 2.93M OP units are treated as shares (redeemable 1:1); the Series I preferred and the $12.5M real-estate-entity NCI are immaterial but excluded from the bridge

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of (regular close, not after-hours); 52-week range 116.17-144.41, so the price sits at the bottom of its range
data_sources.financials: SEC EDGAR: Form 10-Q for the quarter ended 2026-06-30 (accession 0001193125-26-326153) for the balance sheet, OP units and share repurchases; 8-K ex99.1 earnings releases for Q2-2026 (0001193125-26-323756), FY2025 (0001193125-26-037610), FY2023 (0000950170-24-012216) and FY2021 (0000950170-22-000683) for Core FFO, Core AFFO, recurring capex, net debt and guidance; SEC XBRL companyfacts (CIK 912595) for revenue, SBC, dividends and D&A as carried in MAA_Metrics.csv

inputs.base_revenue_note: FY2025 total revenues (XBRL / 10-K). The engine's 'ebitda_margin_path' is the Core AFFO margin on this revenue line, not EBITDA: FY2025 Core AFFO $913.0M = 41.3% of revenue; FY2026 guidance midpoint $7.50/share x ~119.3M weighted shares+units = ~$894M = 40.2% on revenue growing ~0.7%.
inputs.share_count_basis: 116.015M common shares + 2.930M Class A OP units at 30 June 2026 (Q2-2026 earnings release, 'Period End Shares And Units'). Core AFFO is stated attributable to common shareholders AND unitholders, so the divisor must include the OP units. Held FLAT: SBC is already expensed inside Core AFFO (NAREIT FFO does not add back stock compensation) and MAA is a net repurchaser ($72.8M Q1-26, $50M Q2-26 at $130.66).
inputs.net_debt_note: Held at ZERO in the engine by design: Core AFFO is a post-interest, post-preferred-dividend flow capitalised at the cost of equity, so deducting the $5,640.1M net debt again would double-count it. Actual balance sheet at 30 June 2026 recorded in debt_memo.

debt_memo.source: Q2-2026 earnings release (8-K ex99.1, 0001193125-26-323756) net-debt reconciliation and balance-sheet highlights; 10-Q for the quarter ended 2026-06-30 (0001193125-26-326153)

inputs.fcf_definition: Core AFFO attributable to common shareholders and unitholders, FY2025 = Core FFO $1,048.4M less recurring capital expenditures $135.4M (FY2025 earnings release reconciliation). Already after interest expense, preferred dividends, SBC and recurring capex. Redevelopment capex ($17.4M Q4-25; $42.5M H1-26) and development spend are growth capital funded from the ~20% of Core AFFO retained after the dividend plus debt, and are what the growth path pays for; they are not deducted again.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 cash-flow add-back $18.3M (XBRL ShareBasedCompensation). Recorded as a memo only: NAREIT FFO and MAA's Core FFO/Core AFFO do NOT add SBC back, so it is already expensed in last_fcf and is deducted zero times more (sbc_incl_equity_taxes = 0). House and street bases therefore coincide; band_position is null.
inputs.buyback_note: H1-2026 repurchases: $72.78M Q1 (XBRL PaymentsForRepurchaseOfCommonStock) + $50.0M Q2 (0.38M shares at $130.66, 10-Q note 2). FY2025: $27.2M. Flat count is funded, not a convention.
inputs.horizon_note: FY0 is FY2025 actual; year 1 is FY2026 (guided), years 2-10 are FY2027-FY2035. Valuation date is nine months into FY2026, so discounting the full FY2026 Core AFFO one year is mildly conservative; the Q1-Q3 2026 dividends already paid out most of that flow.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of equity, not WACC, because the capitalised flow is post-interest. USD build: 10-year US Treasury 5.24% (Yahoo ^TNX, 2026-10-01), equity risk premium 4.5%, apartment-REIT beta ~0.85 -> 5.24 + 0.85 x 4.5 = 9.1%, rounded to 9.0%. Cross-check: at the current price (inputs.price_as_of) the stock yields ~5.3% on the $6.12 dividend and ~6.4% on FY26 Core AFFO; a 9.0% CoE with 2.5% terminal growth implies a 15.8x steady-state P/AFFO, in line with where apartment REITs have traded in higher-rate years (2023-2026: 14-18x) and below the 2019-2021 20x+ regime. Single rate across scenarios; risk is carried in the probability weights, not stacked into per-scenario discount rates.
inputs.lease_treatment: Not applicable: MAA is the lessor. Ground-lease expense (immaterial) is inside property operating expenses and therefore inside Core AFFO.
inputs.nci_treatment: OP-unit noncontrolling interest ($136.1M book, 2.93M units) is handled by valuing Core AFFO attributable to shareholders AND unitholders and dividing by shares plus units. Consolidated real-estate-entity NCI ($12.5M book at 30-Jun-26) is immaterial and not bridged. MAA Series I preferred ($8.50 cumulative redeemable) is already deducted before FFO.
inputs.notes: MODEL: REIT Core AFFO capitalisation at cost of equity, run through the Drivers/engine route with net debt held at zero (the GPT.AX/GMG.AX/CHC.AX pattern). Routed via .claude/skills/dcf-methods/SKILL.md 'REIT / property trust' row: MAA is a self-managed US multifamily REIT; reported net income is dominated by $620M+/yr of real-estate depreciation and lumpy disposition gains, OCF less capex is not an owner-FCF series, and EBITDA/EV-based multiples are not how the sector is priced. The engine's components are mapped as: revenue = total property revenue; ebitda_margin_path = Core AFFO margin on revenue; sbc, D&A, capex, tax and working-capital paths = 0 (all already inside Core AFFO, or nil for a REIT). First valuation of this ticker (no MEMORY.md entry). US-GAAP XBRL did not tag total debt (REITs split it across NotesPayable/UnsecuredDebt/SecuredDebt), so debt was read from the Q2-2026 10-Q balance sheet and the earnings-release net-debt reconciliation. Core FFO/Core AFFO are non-GAAP and absent from XBRL; they were read from the FY2021, FY2023, FY2025 and Q2-2026 earnings releases on EDGAR.

bear.narrative: Higher-for-longer rates (10y above 5%) keep cap rates and refinancing costs elevated: ~$900M/yr of 3.9%-coupon debt rolls at 5.5-6%, taking ~60bp/yr off the AFFO margin until FY2029, while a softer labour market and renewed construction starts (financing eases for merchant builders) keep new-lease pricing at or below zero through 2027 and concessions elevated in Phoenix, Charlotte, Raleigh and Savannah. Same-store NOI stays flat-to-negative for two more years; the dividend ($6.12) is covered only ~1.1x on Core AFFO so buybacks stop and development slows. Core AFFO/share troughs ~$7.05 in FY2028 and only regains the FY2023 level ($8.24) around FY2035; terminal 2.0% growth with a 15x cap (Gordon at 9.0%/2.0% is 14.6x, so Gordon binds).

base.ebitda_margin_note: Core AFFO margin on total revenue (see inputs.base_revenue_note). FY26 40.2% ties to the $7.50 guidance midpoint. Recovers ~80bp by FY2029 as same-store NOI turns positive (supply below long-term average for 3+ years per management) and the five lease-up communities stabilise (+$70-75M NOI, ~$0.11/share), net of the refinancing headwind (3.9% average coupon on $5.7B rolling at ~5%+). Flat at 41.0% from FY2029: MAA's FY2019-FY2021 Core AFFO margin was 39-41%.
base.narrative: Revenue +0.7% FY26 (same-store revenue guide +0.1% plus lease-up and FY25 acquisitions), then +2.5%/+3.5%/+4.0% FY27-29 as Sunbelt deliveries fall below long-term averages and new-lease pricing reaccelerates from the Q2-26 inflection (+170bp sequential new-lease improvement), fading to 2.5% nominal. Core AFFO/share FY26E $7.52 -> FY30E $8.75 -> FY35E $10.03 (3.2% CAGR), roughly the pre-COVID 2015-2019 cadence. Terminal 2.5% at a 9.0% cost of equity (15.8x AFFO exit); 18x cap does not bind.

bull.narrative: The supply cliff lands as management describes: absorption outpaces deliveries across the footprint from 2027, blended lease growth returns to 4-5%, occupancy holds ~95.5% and expense growth stays near 1-2%, so same-store NOI compounds mid-single digits for three years. The $800M-$1B development pipeline (5-7 starts/yr) delivers at the stated 6%+ yields against ~5% cap rates. Core AFFO margin expands ~280bp to 43% as operating leverage outruns refinancing cost. Core AFFO/share FY30E ~$9.55, FY35E ~$11.35; terminal 3.0% growth (18x exit, 20x cap not binding).

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 18x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25% because the two dominant axes - the path of long rates and the timing of the Sunbelt supply/demand rebalance - are macro variables MAA cannot control, management has already cut same-store revenue guidance twice in 2026 (midpoint 0.90% -> 0.55% -> 0.10%), and Core AFFO/share has declined three consecutive years. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs the supply decline, demand resilience and benign rates to coincide. Not higher on bear: investment-grade balance sheet, 87% fixed-rate debt and 6-year average maturity mean the downside is slower growth, not distress.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide (SBC immaterial): the band collapsed, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
sanity_check.fy_end_month_source: December (fallback: no fiscal_year_end and no annual filing)
